[element-see-also]
=== `<see-also>` See-Also (in an index-term)

Used only within an embedded index term (<<element-index-term,`<index-term>`>>) to hold non-preferred terms that make “See Also” references when an Index is generated.

#### Usage/Remarks
##### Best Practice

The primary (useful) content of a <<element-see-also,`<see-also>`>> element is one or more <<element-index-term,`<index-term>`>> elements to which the user is being directed. Thus a typical embedded See Also reference would contain only an <<element-index-term,`<index-term>`>>, with words such as “See Also” (or similar) generated by a display application. Many other elements are allowed within a <<element-see-also,`<see-also>`>> element for those rare cases where additional narrative explanation of the index-term is provided.

#### Related Elements

*Not for Terms and Definitions Section:* This is an element, copied from BITS, that is used to generate indexes automatically; this element is _not related_ to the terms and definitions section in a standards document. In the terms and definitions section of a standard, see also entries related to terms are tagged as <<element-related-term,`<related-term>`>> elements with a <<attribute-related-term-type,`@related-term-type`>> attribute describing the relationship.

</sec>
